CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Age: 41 years
Sex: Female
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Follow-up cytogenetic analysis after trisomy 22 detection in recent pregnancy. Previous pregnancy showed trisomy 22 in placental material.

SPECIMEN
Peripheral blood collected on [redacted date]

METHODOLOGY
Targeted G-banded chromosome analysis with specific attention to chromosome 22. Peripheral blood lymphocytes were cultured for 72 hours using standard techniques. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphases were analyzed with particular focus on chromosome 22 structure and number.

RESULTS
Karyotype: 46,XX

No chromosomal rearrangement identified in chromosome 22 analysis. Both copies of chromosome 22 appear structurally normal with no evidence of deletions, duplications, or rearrangements. Previous trisomy 22 in placental material not reflected in maternal karyotype.

INTERPRETATION
The normal female karyotype with structurally normal chromosome 22 homologs indicates that the trisomy 22 identified in the previous pregnancy was likely a sporadic event arising during meiosis or early embryonic development. The absence of chromosomal rearrangements involving chromosome 22 in the maternal karyotype suggests low recurrence risk for future pregnancies.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss:
- The sporadic nature of the previous trisomy 22
- Recurrence risks for future pregnancies
- Prenatal testing options for subsequent pregnancies
- Advanced maternal age considerations

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
